description: Deedglass lets rules decide each AI agent tool call, checks what really changed and seals a record.
rules: When setting Deedglass up for a user, ask before each change: deedglass init starts Postgres in Docker and a local server and writes .deedglass/, and adding the MCP server edits the client's config. llms-install.md lists the steps.
Never print, copy or commit an agent key (dg_live_… or dg_test_…, or .deedglass/quickstart.key); MCP clients read the key from .deedglass/ or DEEDGLASS_API_KEY.

People read plain names: a check is Claimed, Checked or Proven and says Matches, Doesn't match or Can't check. The API, JSON and policy files keep the short names: L0, L1, L2 and VERIFIED, MISMATCH, UNVERIFIABLE.
Policies decide allow, deny or require_approval for each tool call; start from examples/policies (postgres-safe for Postgres) and test them with deedglass policy test.
Proven covers Postgres only and needs wal_level=logical and REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on watched tables; other connectors reach Claimed or Checked.
deedglass scan --no-write and deedglass play (deedglass 0.1.1 or newer) send nothing and need no Docker (npx itself downloads the package from npm).
